meta.scope: South Korea Batch 6 — Environmental statistics & key environmental agreements, additional financial depth, and the international commercial / industrial / treaty architecture (FTA network overview, major multilateral memberships, investment treaties context). Addresses user request for environmental, detailed financial, and comprehensive international agreements coverage under the locked definition.
meta.strategy_note: Korea maintains one of the world’s densest FTA networks (20+ FTAs covering 60 countries as of 2026), is an OECD/WTO member, and is party to the major climate and biodiversity instruments. This batch captures the high-value recurring-citation agreements and the official environmental/financial statistical products that support them.

candidates.title: National Greenhouse Gas Inventory (국가 온실가스 인벤토리)
candidates.publisher: Greenhouse Gas Inventory and Research Center of Korea (GIR) / Ministry of Environment
candidates.description: Official annual national greenhouse-gas inventory compiled according to IPCC guidelines. Reports total emissions, sectoral breakdowns (energy, industrial processes, agriculture, LULUCF, waste) and is the empirical basis for NDC tracking and climate-policy evaluation.
candidates.notes: Core environmental statistics node. Continuously cited in climate policy, energy-transition analysis and international reporting under the Paris Agreement. Complements the energy-balance and electricity-generation (including nuclear) series.

candidates.title: Paris Agreement (under UNFCCC) — Korea’s ratification and NDC framework
candidates.description: Korea is a party to the Paris Agreement (ratified). The Agreement and Korea’s successive Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) form the central international climate framework against which domestic GHG inventories, energy plans and industrial decarbonisation measures are assessed.
referenced_by: National Greenhouse Gas Inventory and Biennial Transparency Reports
Energy Master Plans and carbon-neutrality roadmaps
Industrial and power-sector policy documents that reference NDC targets
candidates.notes: Prime recurring-citation climate instrument. Parallel to the environmental dimension of Japan’s Strategic Energy Plan cluster.

candidates.title: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and related biodiversity instruments (incl. BBNJ ratification)
candidates.description: Korea is party to the Convention on Biological Diversity and has ratified the Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ / High Seas Treaty), becoming the first East Asian country to do so. These instruments frame domestic biodiversity and marine-conservation policy.
referenced_by: National biodiversity strategies and marine-protected-area policy
Environmental white papers and related statistical products
candidates.notes: Key environmental-agreement cluster. BBNJ ratification is a recent high-profile step.

candidates.title: Korea’s FTA Network (overview of FTAs in force)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources (MOTIR) / Korea Customs Service
candidates.description: As of 2026 Korea has 23 FTAs in force covering approximately 60 countries. Major partners include Chile (first FTA, 2004), Singapore, EFTA, ASEAN, India (CEPA), EU, Peru, United States (KORUS), Türkiye, Australia, Canada, China, Vietnam, Colombia, New Zealand, Central America, United Kingdom, RCEP, Indonesia, Israel, Cambodia, Philippines, UAE and others. The network is one of the densest among major economies.
referenced_by: MOTIR and Customs FTA utilisation and trade statistics
Trade-policy white papers and impact assessments
Individual FTA legal texts and subsequent review processes
candidates.notes: Meta-node that captures the overall architecture. Individual high-impact FTAs (KORUS, Korea–EU, RCEP) already have dedicated nodes in Batch 2; this node situates them inside the full network and supports analysis of Korea’s multi-track trade strategy.

candidates.title: China–Korea Free Trade Agreement
candidates.publisher: Governments of the Republic of Korea and the People’s Republic of China
candidates.description: Bilateral FTA that entered into force in December 2015. Covers goods, services and investment between Korea and its largest single trading partner.
referenced_by: Trade statistics on China partner share
Industrial and supply-chain analysis involving China
candidates.notes: High-volume bilateral instrument. Complements KORUS, Korea–EU and RCEP in the core trade-agreement set.

candidates.title: Korea–ASEAN FTA (goods, services, investment)
candidates.publisher: Republic of Korea and ASEAN Member States
candidates.description: Framework of agreements on goods (in force 2007), services (2009) and investment (2009) between Korea and the ten ASEAN members. Foundational regional economic partnership that predates RCEP.
candidates.notes: Important regional pillar. Many subsequent bilateral ASEAN-country FTAs and RCEP build on this foundation.

candidates.title: OECD membership and WTO membership
candidates.description: Korea has been a member of the OECD since 1996 and is a founding member of the WTO (1995). These memberships structure a wide range of statistical reporting, peer reviews, trade-policy commitments and regulatory alignment.
referenced_by: OECD Economic Surveys of Korea and statistical reporting
Domestic policy documents that reference OECD/WTO norms
candidates.notes: Institutional membership nodes that underwrite statistical quality, policy peer review and the rules-based trading system in which Korea operates.

candidates.title: Bilateral Investment Treaties (BITs) and investment-protection network
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Republic of Korea
candidates.description: Korea has concluded bilateral investment treaties with approximately 100 countries (around 84 in force as of mid-2025). Together with the investment chapters of its FTAs, these instruments form the legal framework for outbound and inbound investment protection.
referenced_by: Investment statistics and FDI policy documents
FTA investment chapters and dispute-settlement references
candidates.notes: Complements the FTA network. The dense BIT web is relevant to Korea’s role as both a major outward investor and a destination for FDI in manufacturing and technology.

candidates.title: Financial Stability Report and related BOK financial-system statistics
candidates.description: Periodic Financial Stability Report together with underlying statistics on household debt, corporate credit, bank soundness, non-bank financial institutions and systemic-risk indicators.
candidates.notes: Deepens the financial cluster beyond monetary aggregates and Flow of Funds. Household debt and real-estate-linked leverage are major structural issues in Korea; these reports and statistics are continuously cited in macro-prudential and housing-policy analysis.

candidates.title: External debt and foreign-reserve statistics
candidates.publisher: Bank of Korea (BOK) / Ministry of Economy and Finance
candidates.description: Statistics on gross and net external debt by sector and maturity, together with official foreign-exchange reserve holdings and related external-vulnerability indicators.
candidates.notes: Complements the Balance of Payments and international-investment-position series. Important for assessing external resilience in an open, export-oriented economy.
